transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep rechecking my work on jobs. Like breakers, labels, torque marks, photos—stuff I know I already checked. Sometimes I’ll even drive back to a site to look again. A simple install ends up taking way longer than it should, and people are starting to notice.
Do you feel anxious or worried when you don’t recheck your work, or does it feel like something bad might happen if you don’t?

Yeah. Even when I know I already checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought keeps pushing in like, what if I missed a loose neutral, or left something that could start a fire. I try to tell myself it’s fine and let it go, but it kind of follows me all the way home.
Do these thoughts about missing something feel like they don’t belong to you or feel out of control, like they’re invading your mind even though you don’t want them?

Yeah, that’s pretty much it. It feels like it barges in even after I know I checked it. I’ll be thinking, maybe I missed one loose neutral, or maybe something could heat up and start a fire. I don’t want to keep thinking about it, and I try to shake it off, but it follows me home anyway.
Do you perform any specific actions or rituals to try to reduce the worry or make sure nothing bad happens after you have these thoughts?

Yes. I’ll go back through the job again—check the breakers, the labels, torque marks, and I’ll look through the photos I took. Sometimes that still doesn’t settle it, and I’ll drive back to the site to check in person. I know it’s too much, but doing it is the only thing that makes the worry ease up for a while.
How much time do these thoughts and checking behaviors take up in your day, and does it interfere with your work or home life?

It can take up a lot of the day, honestly. A job that should be one visit turns into me checking it again, looking through pictures, sometimes making a callback or going back over things. My schedule starts slipping, and I can tell it’s starting to affect how clients see me. It also takes time away from the apprentices because I’m tied up rechecking instead of moving on or teaching.

And at home, I’m not really done with work. I’ll skip stuff I used to enjoy after work because I’m still sitting there reviewing the job in my head or wondering if I need to go back.
